title: Published atom inequality helper: compare exact bytes
security_scope: Adapted port of the exact published != inline helper only. Accepts exactly two atom arguments and returns true precisely when their byte sequences differ. Nil, nonempty zero bytes, padded numeric encodings and arbitrary non-UTF8 bytes remain distinct data. Pair operands and malformed/extra argument lists reject. The visible strict module wrapper is an added ABI contract, not a published standalone module. This pure Boolean helper has no ledger, authorization, cryptographic, constant-time or compiler-preservation claim.

source_adaptation.description: Retain exactly the published inline != helper from relops.clinc line 4. The surrounding module adds explicit proper two-argument environment checks. The helper itself uses not(= A B); CLVM = rejects pair operands and compares all atom bytes. The line-ending newline after the verbatim span belongs to the adapter because the upstream final line has no trailing LF.

limitations: Only the != inline helper on relops.clinc line 4 is adapted. This does not complete the source library, a protocol or a CHIP.
The source is an include helper, not a standalone module with a published artifact; no canonical compiled module hash is claimed.
The explicit strict two-argument module wrapper is an added input contract. Pair arguments reject; every atom byte and length matters, including nil, nonempty zero, padding and invalid UTF-8.
No integer decoding or Unicode normalization is applied. Ordinary Rust u8 slice comparison supplies byte-value equality; this is not general trait-call support.
The result is a Boolean CLVM atom, not spend conditions. There is no ledger, cryptographic authentication or constant-time claim.
Host and VM resource limits must not be counted as program rejection. Finite cross-language comparisons do not establish compiler preservation or universal resource equivalence.
